tagline: Twelve miles up the street that splits Baltimore east from west.
intro: Charles Street starts in South Baltimore by Federal Hill, runs north past the Inner Harbor and up through downtown, divides around the park squares of Mount Vernon Place, and carries on past Johns Hopkins and the wooded neighborhoods of the north end into Baltimore County, ending at Lutherville about 12 miles out. Old churches line the downtown blocks, the Basilica among them.
It was laid out in 1730 as Forest Street. It is also the city's dividing line. A street that crosses it starts its house numbers over and turns from West to East on the way across.

moments.title: Washington Monument, Mount Vernon Place
moments.text: Robert Mills began this 178-foot column in 1815, before he designed the one in Washington. A 16-foot Washington stands on top, 227 steps up.

moments.title: Charles Village
moments.text: Developed in the late 1800s as one of Baltimore's first suburbs, with St. Paul Street, the southbound half of the byway, as its main commercial street.

moments.title: Homewood Museum
moments.text: A wedding gift from Charles Carroll, signer of the Declaration, to his son. The house cost four times its budget and opened a severe breach between them.
